subject: Computer Networking
title: BGP and Autonomous Systems
description: A short lesson to help you apply BGP and Autonomous Systems.

hook.text: By the late 1980s, the internet was many networks. They needed a way to share route information at their borders.

buildup.text: BGP — Border Gateway Protocol — was introduced in 1989. Each network, called an AS, announces its reachable addresses.

discovery.text: BGP lets each AS choose paths based on policy, not just shortest distance. Business relationships influence routing.

twist.text: BGP was built on trust. A misconfigured AS can accidentally hijack traffic for millions of users.

climax.text: BGP still runs the internet's core routing today. It's been patched and extended, never replaced.

punchline.text: BGP holds the internet together with trust and announcements.

quiz.question: What does BGP manage between autonomous systems?
options: Assignment of IP addresses to devices

details.summary: The Border Gateway Protocol, introduced in 1989, enables autonomous systems to exchange routing information and determine paths across the internet.
details.whyItMatters: BGP is the protocol that makes the internet a single interconnected network rather than thousands of separate ones. Without BGP, there would be no internet as we know it.
takeaways: BGP connects autonomous systems into one internet
It operates on trust between network operators
BGP routing decisions affect global internet traffic flow

faq.question: What is an autonomous system?
faq.answer: An autonomous system is a network or group of networks under single administrative control with a unified routing policy. Each ISP, large company, or cloud provider operates one or more autonomous systems. BGP enables these independent systems to route traffic between each other.

faq.question: Why is BGP's trust model considered a weakness?
faq.answer: BGP was designed when the internet was small and operators trusted each other. Any network can announce routes it should not, accidentally or maliciously redirecting traffic. RPKI provides cryptographic verification but adoption is incomplete. BGP hijacks remain a real threat.
